fixes.explanation: That's it, baker. Matthew says that when morning came, all the chief priests and elders of the people conspired against Jesus "…to put Him to death." (Matthew 27:1) Notice it's all of them, not just a few.

Yes, baker. Matthew says Judas "…was filled with remorse…" when he saw that Jesus was condemned. (Matthew 27:3) Remorse is a heavy, sinking kind of feeling, and I think this was a heavy moment for him. The same verse says he returned the thirty pieces of silver to the chief priests and elders.

Not joy, baker. The text says Judas "…was filled with remorse…" (Matthew 27:3) Remorse is sorrow over something done, which is a different feeling from joy. The same verse says he returned the thirty pieces of silver to the chief priests and elders.

That's a fair guess, baker, but it's not the word Matthew uses. He says Judas "…was filled with remorse…" (Matthew 27:3) Remorse is sorrow over what someone has done. The same verse says he returned the thirty pieces of silver.

They don't say that, baker. Judas says he betrayed "innocent blood," and they answer, "What is that to us?" (Matthew 27:4) Then they add, "You bear the responsibility." The text records no agreement from them.

Yes, baker. Matthew says "…Judas threw the silver into the temple and left." (Matthew 27:5) He had come to return it to the chief priests and elders, and this is what he did with it before he left. The silver didn't go home with him.
No hiding in this one, baker. The text says Judas "…threw the silver into the temple and left." (Matthew 27:5) I think he was done with that silver. Nothing in the verse says he took any of it home.

That's it, baker. They said, "It is unlawful to put this into the treasury, since it is blood money." (Matthew 27:6) The verse says the chief priests picked up the silver first. Then they spoke about the treasury.

A market would've been a busy place, baker, but that's not it. Matthew says they bought the potter’s field "…as a burial place for foreigners." (Matthew 27:7) That's the plan the text gives for the field. A market isn't mentioned in the verse.
